frontier.hypothesis: Class B is one measurement short of a closed axis: only a REAL control-flow boundary between the copy and the 0x30/0x34 stores (a label/jump that survives to cse pass 2) remains untested.
frontier.mechanism: cse pass 2 respects only genuine block boundaries (CODE_LABEL / JUMP_INSN), not LOOP_END notes; a real boundary would keep the two pseudos in different quantities all the way to RA and give the free split. The target's asm is straight-line there, so such a boundary cannot be free in instructions.
frontier.next_probe: Spend at most ONE probe: a real branch (e.g. a genuine early-out) between the copy and the stores, measured for insn count. Then treat class B as closed and move to class C or class A. Do NOT re-open note fences, store-base spellings, canonical naming/ordering, the promotion lever, or hard-reg addressing - all measured dead in s7/s8.

frontier.hypothesis: Class C (rows 62-64) closes if the +0x6A / +0x7E constants can be kept OFF the shift operand while the shift stays the canonical pointer operand of the plus at insn 173.
frontier.mechanism: Pointer-domain PLUS canonicalises to (base, offset) and keeps the row-60 re-read; int-domain PLUS preserves written order but lets cse forward the loop-top base local and delete the re-read. E4 keeps the re-read and flips the order but folds 0x6A/0x7E onto the shift operand before the add, costing one insn (176).
frontier.next_probe: Attack the constant fold, not the operand order: index the row through a struct or array element type so +0x6A is a member offset rather than a folded addend, or give the two inner-loop pointers a common (u8 *)(t0*10) + (s32)D_800A36A0 row whose two users each add their own constant. Read text1b.rtl for E4 (tmp/grind/func_800770B8/s6/v/E4.c) against the baseline dumps in tmp/grind/func_800770B8/dumps/.

frontier.hypothesis: Class A (prologue rows 7-12, 4 of the 8 real residual rows) is the largest untouched residual and has never had its sched2 decision read out of a dump.
frontier.mechanism: The register-save stores do not exist until after reload, so the ordering of {sw $ra, sw $s1, addiu $a1 0x1008, lui/lw D_800A374C, addiu $s1,$s0,0x58} is decided by the second scheduling pass; s5 closed the fence hypothesis (the target's prologue is straight-line, and a real first-statement loop costs +11 insns) but nobody has compared our .sched2 ready-list order against the target's emission order.
